summary: Clarify rate-smoothing interaction with mixed ingress (WS + HTTP) and active health probes causing unexpected 429s
description:
Issue summary: Customer reports intermittent 429s in their dedicated pool after enabling 'window_smoothing' for rate limiting. Traffic mix: low-latency websocket sessions (chat) + scheduled HTTP batch uploads. They also have aggressive service health probes (30s cadence) hitting an internal probe path. Impact: customer reports ~0.8% of websocket connections receiving 429s during morning ingest window; business impact includes degraded UX for live chats and delayed batch backfills.

Observed behavior: 429s spike aligns with the customer's batch coordinator starting scheduled jobs and with the probe heartbeats; spikes persist for ~2-3 minutes then decay. Console shows token bucket credits appear to refill but connections still receive 429s until smoothing window completes.

Environment: Dedicated pool (dedicated capacity, single tenant), prod us-west region, model pinned to redwood-rlhf-3b, route uses priority_class=interactive for websockets and priority_class=bulk for batch uploads.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) In dedicated pool, enable rate-limiter feature flag 'window_smoothing: true' with smoothing_window=60s
2) Start a sustained websocket chat workload (50 concurrent short sessions, 1 request/sec each),
3) Kick off a scheduled HTTP batch worker that performs short high-throughput uploads for 90s
4) Ensure health-check probes are enabled on a distinct probe endpoint with 30s interval
5) Observe 429s in websocket clients correlated with batch start and probe pulses
logs:
[2026-03-10T09:02:11Z] ingress(rate-limiter): key=acct-xyz token_bucket=0/120 refill_ts=2026-03-10T09:03:11Z decision=REJECT code=429 route=/ws/chat session_id=abc123
[2026-03-10T09:02:12Z] probe: /health/internal 200 (probe) src=10.8.4.22
[2026-03-10T09:04:05Z] ingress(rate-limiter): key=acct-xyz token_bucket=12/120 decision=ALLOW route=/ws/chat latency=42ms
investigation_notes:
Initial hypothesis: smoothing window is amortizing refill credits across the tenant but health probes and mixed ingress are causing token accounting to be misattributed to the interactive route. We can reproduce in staging with a simplified probe + batch workload. Observed that the rate-limiter central counter applies smoothing at the tenant level and then enforces per-route windows; a small race appears when a probe request drains a tiny portion of a freshly-scheduled refill, pushing some low-latency requests to 429 until the smoothing window restores full per-route capacity.

Telemetry checked: token refill events are emitted, but the 'route_weight' attribution for probe vs interactive was defaulting to weight=1 for the probe route. Weighting the probe lower or excluding probe path from quota accounting mitigates reproduction.

Hypotheses considered:
- health probes counted as normal traffic and unfairly consumed short-window credits (likely)
- smoothing algorithm incorrectly delays per-route refill visibility (possible race)
- dedicated-pool autoscaler interactions (unlikely for this short window)

Next steps: capture full rate-limiter trace around refill boundaries; add temporary probe exclusion rule for customer to validate workaround; propose a short-term config doc update for excluding internal probes from tenant accounting.

resolution:
Workaround applied: we recommended and helped customer add a routing exception to exclude /health/internal from tenant token accounting (route weight=0). Customer validated immediate reduction in websocket 429s.

Permanent recommendations: 1) Add a route-level config 'exclude_from_quota: true' for internal probes and monitoring endpoints; 2) Provide sample rate-smoothing parameter guidance in Console: smoothing_window=60s for mixed traffic, probe route weight <=0.1; 3) PR to runtime to emit clearer metrics when smoothing is active and to make per-route refill visibility consistent (linked PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/rate-limiter/pull/1123).

Follow-ups: Engineering to review race around per-route refill visibility (owner: @ramey). Docs/Support to publish KB article 'Avoiding probe-induced 429s with window smoothing' and add recommended default for dedicated pools. Marking ticket Resolved once docs PR lands.
